golden_baseline_location: deterministic legacy run: OTTERWORKS_LEGACY_ROOT=<root> make legacy-etl-gen-data NS=cnvfinance; make legacy-etl-run JOB=sftp_ingest_poll; JOB=parse_custbill_fixedwidth; TP_FAKETIME='2026-01-15 00:00:00' JOB=finance_excel_report -> reports/finance_billing_20260115.csv (sha256 ef1ad83223ebf1e902d57b15126f63fed91510b3228e8883d3c1bb6f03cadde0); empty-input baseline: same finance job on a fresh empty root -> header-only CSV (sha256 4cbc4f1506b7f1cc335237cc23573b18944f38c349f11a94d47157ee464671ea)

acceptance_checks.description: gold.finance_billing_summary_cnvfinance for the report date contains exactly the golden CSV's currency x record-type grid: same 6 rows, record_count equal and total_amount equal to the cent (exact decimal comparison, no float tolerance).
gold totals equal an aggregation recomputed directly from silver.custbill_records_cnvfinance, and sum(record_count) equals the golden total (100), so gold cannot drift from silver.
gold.finance_report_delivery_cnvfinance has exactly one row per (ns, report_date) whose status records verified volume delivery and the explicit absence of a mail transport - never a pretended send.
the emitted artifact is a real CSV with a .csv extension whose bytes equal the golden legacy report; the CSV-renamed-.xls defect is not reproduced.
an actual job rerun replaces the (ns, report_date) slice: the summary grid is identical before and after and row count does not grow.
a run over an empty input directory succeeds, yields zero summary rows for its report date and a header-only artifact byte-identical to the empty-input golden baseline.

planted_anomalies.description: record type outside 01/02 must surface as UNKNOWN(rt), as the legacy report did
planted_anomalies.reason: gen_sample_data.pl emits only record types 01 and 02 for this namespace; the UNKNOWN(rt) mapping is implemented and covered by code but never exercised by planted data.

planted_anomalies.description: rows with an empty customer id are skipped and attributed, never aggregated
planted_anomalies.reason: the deterministic generator never emits an empty customer id; the skip-and-count path is implemented but not exercised by planted data.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: ASCII (parser output is 7-bit; generator emits ASCII only)
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: landing transport is byte-exact (Files API PUT of the .psv bytes); parsing decodes as UTF-8 which is a superset of the ASCII the chain produces
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: none can occur from the deterministic generator; a genuinely invalid byte would surface as a malformed row and be counted, not silently coerced

malformed_record_policy.details: matching perl's list-assignment from split(/|/), fields beyond the sixth are ignored; rows with an empty/NULL customer id are skipped and counted in the delivery audit (legacy: next if $cust eq '') ; non-numeric amounts and truncated lines with a missing/empty currency or record type are excluded and counted in rows_attributed_malformed rather than coerced or grouped under an empty key - NULL or missing values never fail open into a plausible row; input files are selected by the legacy CUSTBILL*.psv filename filter.

empty_input_semantics.details: legacy runs mkdir -p on the parsed dir before opendir, so an empty OR missing parsed dir both yield a header-only report and exit 0 (the opendir die is only reachable for an existing-but-unlistable dir); the converted job mirrors this: it creates the input directory if absent, an input directory with no CUSTBILL files clears the (ns, report_date) summary slice, writes a header-only CSV artifact and records the delivery, and a directory that exists but cannot be listed fails the run before any destructive delete. land --allow-empty materialises the empty directory explicitly.
